hints.content:
Figures are congruent if we can map one onto the other using rigid transformations.

So we want to show we can map angle $x$ onto angle $y$, or vice versa, using rigid transformations.

## A translation along the directed line segment $AC$



[[☃ image 1]]

This translation maps line $\overrightarrow{AB}$ onto line $\overrightarrow{CD}$, but it doesn't map angle $x$ onto angle $y$, so this transformation did not give us the information we needed for the proof.

options.alt: Parallel lines A B and C D. There is an intersecting line that runs diagonally up and right through points B and C. Point E lies on line C D and Point F lies on the transversal. The transversal line creates several angles. Angle A B C is labeled X, and  Angle A B C is the top left interior angle. Angle E C F is labeled Y. Angle E C F is the bottom left exterior angle. The parallel lines and transversal are then translated down so that line A prime B prime maps onto line C D. There are arrows showing the movement of each line. A prime maps onto point C. The angles X and Y do not map onto each other.

hints.content:
## A translation along the directed line segment $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

This translation maps lines $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ onto themselves. It doesn't map angle $x$ onto angle $y$ or vice versa. So this transformation did not give us the information we needed for the proof.

options.alt: Parallel lines A B and C D. There is an intersecting line that runs diagonally up and right through points B and C. Point E lies on line C D and Point F lies on the transversal. The transversal line creates several angles. Angle A B C is labeled X, and  Angle A B C is the top left interior angle. Angle E C F is labeled Y. Angle E C F is the bottom left exterior angle. The parallel lines are then translated onto themselves to the right so that line A prime B prime maps onto line A B. The transversal is translated to the right. There are arrows showing the movement of each line. A prime maps onto point B. B prime maps further right on line A B. The angles X and Y do not map onto each other.

hints.content:
## A translation along the directed line segment $CB$



[[☃ image 1]]

Yes! We mapped angle $y$ onto angle $x$.

"A translation along the directed line segment $CB$ maps line $\overleftrightarrow{CD}$ onto line $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ and angle $y$ onto angle $x$."

This is the valid proof.

options.alt: Parallel lines A B and C D. There is an intersecting line that runs diagonally up and right through points B and C. Point E lies on line C D and Point F lies on the transversal. The transversal line creates several angles. Angle A B C is labeled X, and  Angle A B C is the top left interior angle. Angle E C F is labeled Y. Angle E C F is the bottom left exterior angle. The parallel lines and transversal are then translated up so that line C prime D prime maps onto line A B. There are arrows showing the movement of each line. C prime maps onto point B. D prime maps further right on line A B. Line A prime B prime is above line A B. Angle Y maps onto angle X.

question.content:
$\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overleftrightarrow{CD}$ are parallel lines.



[[☃ image 1]]

**Which translation of the plane can we use to prove angles $x$ and $y$ are congruent, and why?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: Parallel lines A B and C D. There is an intersecting line that runs diagonally up and right through points B and C. Point E lies on line C D and Point F lies on the transversal. The transversal line creates several angles. Angle A B C is labeled X, and  Angle A B C is the top left interior angle. Angle E C F is labeled Y. Angle E C F is the bottom left exterior angle.

choices.content: A translation along the directed line segment $CB$ maps line $\overleftrightarrow{CD}$ onto line $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ and angle $y$ onto angle $x$.
A translation along the directed line segment $AC$ maps line $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ onto line $\overleftrightarrow{CD}$ and angle $x$ onto angle $y$.
A translation along the directed line segment $AB$ maps line $\overleftrightarrow{CD}$ onto line $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ and angle $y$ onto angle $x$.
